 Daily Stock Market Live
 Updated Wed, Nov 18 2026 5:13 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow drops more than 500 points; S&P 500 falls for fifth day as Nvidia sells off
 Sean Conlon Ananya Chetia Lim Hui Jie Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, Nov. 17, 2026 in New York City. Spencer Platt | Getty Images The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell on Wednesday as Nvidia shares lost momentum following the chipmaker's better-than-expected earnings report.
 The 30-stock index shed 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to end at 50,198.17. The S&P 500 lost 0.23% and closed at 7,323.63. It was the fifth consecutive losing session for the broad market index and its longest slide since June. The Nasdaq Composite outperformed and rose 0.42% to 24,429.88.
 Shares of Nvidia were 2.9% lower, reversing course from earlier gains after the company's profit and revenue in the third quarter beat analysts' estimates. The company also lifted its revenue guidance for the fiscal year ending January 2028, calling for 75% growth year over year.
 The report marked the chipmaker's first since Jensen Huang resigned last week as CEO, a move that came days after he admitted to an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The company's board chair, Harvey Jones, said at the start of the earnings call that the board doesn't intend to bring Huang back as chief executive.
 "It's going to be an adjustment, but it's one that the market will work its way through, just as it always has in the past," said Eric Parnell, chief market strategist at Great Valley Advisor Group.
 When it comes to the broader artificial intelligence trade, however, Parnell noted that the underlying fundamental challenges, including those related to capital expenditures and debt financing, haven't changed — and might not anytime soon.
 "It doesn't take much of a slowdown in earnings growth in the environment that we're in with the AI buildout and the AI spend to take these types of stocks down pretty quickly," he said. "It's this type of volatility that I suspect we're not only going to continue to see but it's likely to increase as we go through 2027 and into 2028."
 The Dow was also weighed down by losses in healthcare stocks like UnitedHealth as well as energy name Chevron and industrial giant Caterpillar . UnitedHealth lost 10%, while Chevron and Caterpillar declined almost 4% and more than 2%, respectively.
 On Tuesday, the blue-chip index dropped more than 1%, while the S&P 500 notched its lowest closing level since July 29. The Nasdaq shed almost 1% and touched its lowest level since April during the session.
 Investors are looking ahead to a blockbuster initial public offering from Anthropic later this week. The AI giant's shares are expected to be priced above the current range between $70 and $78, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
 1 Hour Ago Dow, S&P 500 finish lower
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed lower on Wednesday.
 The 30-stock index lost 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to close at 50,198.17, while the broad market S&P 500 dipped 0.23% to 7,323.63.
 The Nasdaq Composite, however, rose 0.42% to end the day at 24,429.88.
 — Sean Conlon 
 3 Hours Ago Investors could be 'underestimating' AI competition from China, UBS says
 The stock market might not be fully acknowledging the threat China poses to the U.S.'s standing in the artificial intelligence race, according to UBS.
 "US AI leadership remains powerful, but we heard that the market may be underestimating Chinese competition and the potential fragmentation of corporate demand," said strategist Reinout De Bock in a Tuesday note.
 "The question is not just how quickly AI capex grows, but who will own the infrastructure, control the data and capture the monetization," he added.
 — Sean Conlon 
 3 Hours Ago Fed minutes show officials expect more rate hikes
 Kevin Warsh, chairman of the US Federal Reserve, during a news conference following a Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. Daniel Heuer | Bloomberg | Getty Images Federal Reserve officials expressed confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to stem inflation, though they decided to hold off while gathering more information, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday.
 Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk."
 More broadly, officials said "inflation pressures in the economy were broad based" and would warrant action, with "some" policymakers advocating for a quarter percentage point hike at the meeting. A couple participants even noted the possibility that a larger increase might be needed at the next policy meeting in December.
 The meeting summary said "almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate … would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective."
 Read the full story here .
 — Jeff Cox 
 5 Hours Ago Energy stocks slide as oil prices fall
 ExxonMobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Wednesday, May 6, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Energy stocks fell alongside oil prices as investors reacted to last week's rise in U.S. crude and fuel inventories , even though tensions between the U.S. and Iran persist.
 Shares of ExxonMobil and Chevron each dropped more than 3%, while others like ConocoPhillips and EOG Resources were down more than 2%.
 S&P 500 energy was the worst performing sector during the session, falling nearly 3%.
 That's as crude oil prices were lower on the day. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell more than 4% to $82.19 per barrel. International benchmark Brent crude futures slid more than 2% to $90.83 per barrel.
 — Sean Conlon 
 5 Hours Ago Target shares jump 6% after retailer reports best sales growth in five years
 Target on Wednesday reported its best sales growth in more than five years and beat Wall Street's revenue expectations, the latest signs of its turnaround strategy taking hold.
 The retailer said its net sales grew 7.1% during the fiscal third quarter. Comparable sales rose 5.6%, compared with StreetAccount estimates of up 3.8%. That growth was boosted by a 5% increase in comparable traffic, Target added. 
 ″[It's] a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often," CEO Michael Fiddelke told reporters. Read more .
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon TGT, 1-day — Laya Neelakandan 
 6 Hours Ago SpaceX may start separating from the AI trade, Morgan Stanley says
 Visual China Group | Getty Images SpaceX shares are up more than 3% over the last five sessions as of late morning trading Wednesday, while the Nasdaq Composite is down more than 4%. That separation may be a sign of things to come, according to Morgan Stanley. 
 "As the AI trade diffuses into its next era, we see scope for further decorrelation and a more durable place in investor portfolios," analyst Adam Jonas wrote in a Tuesday note about SpaceX shares. 
 Two key things lead Jonas to this prediction: revenue from the company's connectivity — Starlink — vertical, the increasing need for SpaceX's Terafab as the U.S. seeks to create a more independent semiconductor supply chain.
 However, a merger between SpaceX and Tesla, Elon Musk's other megacap company, creates a ceiling for the former's stock for now, he said. "Most investors we speak with are broadly comfortable with the merits of a potential combination," Jonas wrote, "but put off by the lack of certainty on timing and potential dilution risk."
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon SpaceX 5-day. — Davis Giangiulio 
 7 Hours Ago Anthropic proxies gain ahead of IPO 
 Anthropic proxies gained ahead of the company's IPO. Here are some of the moves: 
 Shares of Amazon and Alphabet rallied 2% and nearly 1%, respectively. The two companies are direct proxies for Anthropic, given their independent investments in the AI company. In April, Amazon agreed to invest up to $25 billion in the company. That same month, Google said it plans to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic , expanding on a longstanding partnership between the two companies. 
 Broadcom jumped almost 3%. The chipmaker is a major partner of Anthropic, having announced a special purpose vehicle to finance $63 billion in chips and networking products to be leased to Anthropic. 
 — Sarah Min 
 7 Hours Ago Enthusiasm among retail investors for Anthropic IPO could eclipse SpaceX debut
 Silas Stein | Picture Alliance | Getty Images Retail investor Dan Shetty is so eager to get in on the Anthropic initial public offering that he "drained" his Roth IRA and moved roughly $12,000 from Fidelity to Robinhood for a chance to participate.
 "I don't want to tell my grandkids that I didn't invest in Anthropic and I didn't invest in OpenAI during the AI bubble," he said.
 Shetty's enthusiasm is shared by many, with excitement among small investors for the blockbuster IPO expected to be off the charts. Vanda Research estimates that Anthropic could see approximately $250 million of retail net buying when it starts trading Thursday, double the size of SpaceX's IPO.
 "That would be far and away the largest amount of net retail buying of any stock that we've seen in our data on the first day of its listing," Jai Malhi, senior strategist at Vanda, said in an interview with CNBC.
 Read the full story here .
 — Sean Conlon 
 8 Hours Ago S&P 500, Nasdaq open higher
 The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite began Wednesday's session in the green.
 The broad market index climbed 0.2% just after the opening bell, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq moved up 0.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 216 points, or 0.4%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 9 Hours Ago Lowe's, Take-Two Interactive and Freeport-McMoRan among the stocks making premarket moves
 Lowe's : Shares declined more than 3% in premarket trading Wednesday after it reported third-quarter financial results .
 Take-Two Interactive : The stock popped nearly 7% ahead of the company's release of the much-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" game.
 Miners: Spot gold prices were off more than 2% on Wednesday and hit their lowest levels since September 2025 . Shares of some miners declined with the previous metal. Newmont Corporation fell 3%, while Freeport-McMoRan declined 2.5%.
 Check out CNBC's live blog here to read more about the stocks making moves before the bell.
 — Davis Giangiulio and Fred Imbert 
 9 Hours Ago Fed may need to 'shock people' with 50 basis-point rate increase, Waller says
 Federal Reserve Board Governor Christopher Waller speaks prior to giving a Reuters NEXT Newsmaker interview in Washington, D.C., US, September 3, 2026. Kylie Cooper | Reuters Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation, which he said has been more persistent than he expected.
 In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half-percentage-point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
 From here, he said the Fed needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more.
 "You might need to, like, shock people," Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman during the "Squawk Box" interview.
 Read the full story below.
 Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike — Jeff Cox 
 10 Hours Ago Citi lowers bitcoin and ether target after crypto sell-off
 People walk past a neon sign advertising a Bitcoin and Ethereum crypto currency exchange in Warsaw, Poland on 19 May, 2024.  Jaap Arriens | Nurphoto | Getty Images The recent crypto sell-off has led Citi to trim its targets for bitcoin and ether. 
 "We revise our base-case price targets for BTC and ETH to $99,532 and $2,838, respectively, as crypto's holding pattern has broken to the downside, with both assets down since our last update. BTC's break below its 200-day moving average prompts us to cut our near-term flow outlook to neutral," wrote strategist Alex Saunders. "ETF demand has deteriorated, with BTC flows slipping back into year-to-date net outflows and ETH recording outflows in each of the past seven weeks, while futures positioning points to deleveraging across tokens."
 Bitcoin has fallen more than 14% over the past week, following the S&P 500 lower. Ether lost more than 13% in that time.
 "The macro backdrop has tightened via a stronger dollar, higher real yields and a spike in equity volatility, and BTC's correlation to the S&P 500 is back above gold," he said.
 — Fred Imbert 
 12 Hours Ago Nvidia ‘uninvestable’: Fund manager
 Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Questar Capital Partners, said in a note Wednesday that Nvidia is "uninvestable." 
 "Nvidia is the Jenga tower of the whole AI trade, and that is not a compliment," he said. "A week ago, we thought this was a pedestrian story about a CEO whose ego got the best of him. Then we found out there was no clear succession plan, and poor corporate governance, with no Chairman until this scandal came to light."
 He added that Nvidia's delayed 10-Q was a "red flag, as it's out of character from its previous releases."
 "We believe there are significant questions about where Nvidia has been selling its chips," Reyle said. "For investors who own the stock, this is an immediate sell in our view. We have never owned Nvidia and believe the stock has been and remains uninvestable."
 Shares of Nvidia were up around 4% in pre-market trading on Wednesday. 
 "There's another company set to begin a spectacular run (Anthropic), and every moment spent worrying about Nvidia is time that could have been spent finding the next winner," Reyle added. "News flash: NVDA ain't it."
 —  Chloe Taylor 
 12 Hours Ago Nvidia stock up nearly 4% as earnings beat expectations. Neoclouds surge
 Visual China Group | Getty Images Nvidia stock was up nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday after reporting another earnings beat , as the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continues to unfold.
 The chip giant's stock was 3.96% higher at 5.08 a.m. ET on Wednesday in pre-market trading.
 Neoclouds were buoyed by the results. CoreWeave was up 6.2%, Nebius 8.1% and Iren 7.4%.
 — Kai Nicol-Schwarz 
 12 Hours Ago U.S. chip stocks jump in pre-market trading
 U.S.-listed semiconductor stocks rose in pre-market trading Wednesday, following Nvidia's earnings beat. 
 Ahead of the opening bell, Nvidia stock was trading 3.9% higher, with the iShares and VanEck semiconductor ETFs both adding around 2.8%. 
 Marvell Technology added 4.3%, Arm was up by 3.8% and Micron gained 3.6%. KLA Corporation and AMD also traded more than 3% higher. 
 —  Chloe Taylor 
 13 Hours Ago Trump lands in Shenzhen as tech, trade and energy top agenda for historic talks
 US President Donald Trump stands at the top of the stairs of Air Force One as he arrives at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 18, 2026. (Photo by Mandel NGAN / POOL / AFP via Getty Images) Mandel Ngan | Afp | Getty Images President Donald Trump has landed in China for the APEC summit, where he is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in the first trilateral talks between the three leaders on Thursday. 
 The meeting — taking place in Shenzhen, a major tech hub — puts trade and technology in sharp focus. Markets will be watching for any sign of progress on U.S.-China trade tensions or restrictions on advanced AI chips.
 Xi opened the summit by calling for fewer trade and investment barriers and closer cooperation on artificial intelligence.
 Traders are also watching for any signal on Ukraine, sanctions and energy, and the conflict in the Middle East , which could shape expectations for Russian oil exports and the geopolitical risk premium.
 — Hugh Leask 
 14 Hours Ago Precious metals tumble, gold falls to one-year low
 One kilogram and a five hundred gram gold bars next to one kilogram silver bars at The Vaults Group gold dealers arranged in Barcelona, Spain, on Monday, April 28, 2025. Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Precious metals sold off Wednesday morning, with gold falling to its lowest level in over a year and silver also plunging to a 52-week low, as expectations of interest rate rises from the Federal Reserve next month drew investors away from non-interest bearing assets.
 Gold futures fell 2.34% to $3,761.84, while spot gold was down 2.38% at $3,758%. Silver futures slipped 3.5% to $45.72, as spot silver shed 3.6% to reach $45.67.
 Nannette Hechler-Fayd'herbe, Lombard Odier Group's chief investment officer for EMEA and head of investment strategy, sustainability and research, said she remained optimistic on gold over the next 12 months, but warned that investors may need to be patient.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Gold futures. Hechler-Fayd'herbe does not expect the Federal Reserve or other central banks to embark on a sustained series of interest-rate hikes. But with U.S. real yields moving back up to 2.9%, from 2.6% not long ago, conditions are not yet supportive of an immediate rally, she said.
 "This of course is not an environment where gold can immediately perform, so a little bit of patience on gold I think is warranted," she told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday.
 — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago European stock markets open in the red
 European stock markets were largely negative in early trading on Wednesday, with the Stoxx 600 edging just below the flatline shortly after 8:00 a.m. in London (3:00 a.m. E.T.). 
 Technology stocks advanced 1.16%, leading continental sectors, while industrial goods added 0.19%. But most other sectors were in the red, with basic resources tumbling 2.41%, while autos fell 0.43%.
 Germany's DAX was up almost 0.1% in early trading in Frankfurt.
 The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was down 0.32% in London, while in Paris, the CAC 40 was flat. In Milan, the Italian FTSE MIB was hovering just below the flatline.
 — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago Indonesia central bank unexpectedly hikes rates to 6%
 Indonesia's central bank on Wednesday raised rates by 25 basis points in a surprise move, bringing its policy rate to 6% — last seen in December 2024. 
 Economists polled by Reuters had expected the bank to keep rates steady at 5.75%.
 The Bank of Indonesia said the move was to strengthen the currency and a preemptive measure to keep inflation in its target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.
 The Indonesian rupiah depreciated to a record low of 18,285 against the greenback on Tuesday, while the inflation rate in the country was at 3.23% in October. 
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 15 Hours Ago Asia markets end choppy session mostly higher
 Markets in Asia ended mostly higher on Wednesday in choppy trading as investors assessed Nvidia earnings, Japan exports data, and comments from global leaders at the APEC summit in China. 
 South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights rose, rising 2% to 5,067.44. The small-cap Kosdaq also advanced 2% to close at 662.81.
 Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.28% to close at 59,024.28, while the broad-broad Topix lost 0.42% to 3,824. 
 Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.87% lower in its final hour of trade, while the CSI 300 on mainland China advanced 0.18% to 3,983.77. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.69%, marking a fifth straight day of losses.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 16 Hours Ago UK inflation hits 1-year high as traders bet on Bank of England rate hikes
 The U.K.'s consumer price index recorded annual price growth of 3.6% for October, up from 3.5% in September and in line with expectations, the country's Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday. 
 The reading marks a one-year high and will likely cement expectations for a 25 basis point interest rate hike at the Bank of England's December meeting. 
 18 Hours Ago Nvidia earnings lift Asian tech heavyweights 
 Major Asian tech names gained Wednesday after chip giant Nvidia reported an earnings beat overnight in its first set of results without former CEO Jensen Huang. 
 Memory heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rose 1.21% and 5.1%, respectively, while Japanese semiconductor equipment testers Advantest and Lasertec climbed 4.02% and 4.35%. Tech investor SoftBank Group rose 3.29%.
 Taiwan's TSMC saw a smaller gain, trading just above the flatline.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 18 Hours Ago U.S. oil futures drop 1%, Brent also trades lower
 West Texas Intermediate futures fell 1.06% to $85.13 per barrel on Wednesday.
 Futures for the international benchmark Brent saw a smaller decline, down 0.35% at $92.81 per barrel. 
 The fall in prices comes even as Kuwait reported "hostile drone attacks," with hostilities in the Middle East region appearing to be on the boil again.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 22 Hours Ago Japan's exports growth quicken in October, powered by semiconductors 
 Japan's exports in October surged 20.5% from a year earlier, snapping a two-month slowdown in shipments, official data released Wednesday showed.
 Exports growth beat expectations of economists polled by Reuters that had pegged it at 20%, and it was sharply higher compared to 16.5% in September. 
 Shipments of semiconductor equipment that have been propping up Tokyo's exports jumped 49.7% by value. Exports of motor vehicles climbed 19.9% year on year. 
 In terms of destinations, shipments to China rose 13.3%, while they climbed 23.9% to the U.S. 
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 22 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi leads gains as Asia markets open higher 
 Asia markets opened higher Wednesday, with South Korea leading gains in the region as chip heavyweights soared on Nvidia's earnings beat. 
 The Kospi was 2.9% higher, with heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix climbing 4.47% and 5.83% respectively. Both companies are Nvidia suppliers.
 Japan's Nikkei 225 was up 1.1% after the country reported a sharp 20.5% jump in exports last month, although the broad-based Topix was trading close to the flatline. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.39%.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 23 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei 225 is set to open higher with October trade data in focus
 Asian markets were set to open mixed on Wednesday, after Wall Street closed lower overnight.
 Japan's Nikkei 225 is set for a stronger open, with futures in Chicago at 59,835 and in Osaka last at 58,890 compared to the index Tuesday close of 58,860. The country is set to report October trade data, with Reuters-poll estimates pegging exports growth at 20%. 
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index were last at 23,414, lower than its close of 23,508. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 started the day 0.26% down. 
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 23 Hours Ago Traders shake off WSJ report of SEC investigating Nvidia, shares rise
 Traders appeared to look past a report from The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar, that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating artificial intelligence bellwether Nvidia .
 The Journal's report arrives on the heels of a rocky week for the chip giant, whose CEO Jensen Huang resigned after reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. 
 Shares of Nvidia were last up more than 4% on the back of a third-quarter earnings beat and a strong revenue growth outlook for the fiscal year ending in January 2028.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon nvda — Ananya Chetia 
 24 Hours Ago Stock futures gain Tuesday following Nvidia's strong earnings 
 Stock futures rose on Tuesday after Nvidia reported better-than-expected earnings and strong guidance.
 Nasdaq-100 futures were up 1.37% while S&P 500 futures added 0.82%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures climbed over 170 points or 0.34%. 
 — Ananya Chetia
